headline: Profit and EPS grow as margins tighten, guidance holds
summary_short: Kroger's fiscal Q1 2026 sales rose 2.2% y/y to $46.12 billion and operating profit grew 6.4% y/y to $1.41 billion, while diluted EPS climbed 13.2% y/y to $1.46 even as gross margin compressed 30bp to 22.7%. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance.
summary_long: Sales grew as identical sales ex-fuel rose 1.0% (including a 130bp IRA headwind); ex-fuel/ex-Vitacost sales were up 0.5%. Gross margin fell to 22.7% from 23.0% on higher fuel mix, transportation costs, egg deflation, and price investments, partly offset by pharmacy mix, eCommerce profitability, and sourcing benefits. OG&A rate rose 16bp on wage/hours investment, partly offset by lapping prior-year pension costs. Operating profit still grew, aided by smaller one-off charges than a year ago (2025 carried store-closure and labor-dispute costs). Kroger repurchased $213 million of stock, paid a $0.35/share dividend, and held net debt/adjusted EBITDA at 1.75x. Full-year 2026 guidance for sales, profit, EPS, free cash flow, and capex was reaffirmed unchanged.

drivers.explanation: CEO Foran called the quarter solid but said there is more work to do; the release highlighted adjusted eCommerce sales growth over 19% and Kroger Precision Marketing profit growth over 20%, and reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance.
Growth reflects a 1.0% rise in identical sales ex-fuel (including a 130bp Inflation Reduction Act drag) plus a higher-fuel-sales mix; ex-fuel/ex-Vitacost sales rose only 0.5%.

Gross margin rate fell to 22.7% from 23.0% on higher fuel-sales mix, transportation costs, egg deflation, and planned price investments, partly offset by favorable pharmacy mix, improved eCommerce profitability, and sourcing benefits.

Operating profit grew despite the gross-margin decline and a 16bp OG&A rate increase because last year's quarter carried larger one-off charges (store closures, labor-dispute costs) that mostly lapped out of this year's comparison.
Net income growth trailed operating-profit growth as net interest expense rose to $209M from $199M and the effective tax rate rose to about 23% from 21%, partially offsetting higher pretax income.
EPS rose faster than net income as basic shares outstanding fell to 613 million from 660 million, reflecting ongoing buybacks under the $2 billion authorization approved in December 2025.
Diluted EPS growth mirrors basic EPS: diluted shares fell to 615 million from 664 million on continued share repurchases.
